# The ledger's rules

**Rules version 1.** `sparelimit ledger`, `sparelimit week` and the published numbers carry this number. The rules were written before the work they judge, and they are public so that anyone can read them and re-run them on their own data.

A change to any rule or number below is a new version. The new version is added to [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), and the numbers of every earlier version stay in it exactly as they were. A saving counted under one version is never recounted under another.

## How to re-run them yourself

The rules read two things on your own machine: the audit log Sparelimit wrote when it warned you (`~/.sparelimit/audit.jsonl`) and your session logs. Nothing is sent anywhere.

```bash
sparelimit ledger            # every alert, how it ended, and the counted saving
sparelimit ledger --json     # the same, with the rules version and the before/after numbers behind each saving
sparelimit week --days=0     # the summary over everything on the machine
```

## The rules

### What counts as one alert

Alerts are the warnings Sparelimit wrote to its audit log: the cache-cold nudge, the context-reset nudge, the context-window warning and the plan-limit warnings. Repeats of the same kind within 30 minutes are one alert (plan-limit warnings from every session together; the others per session). Every alert ends in exactly one of: counted, ignored, no-data, pending, stopped, overlap.

### Reset alerts (context reset nudge, context window warning)

Acted on if the context fell to 65% of what it was or less within 15 responses after the alert (a /compact), or a new conversation started in the same project within 60 minutes at 50% of the old context or less. Fewer than 5 responses before the alert: no-data. The saving is the mean cost per response over the 10 responses before the alert, minus the mean over the next 30 after the action, times those responses; fewer than 10 responses after the action: no-data. Not acted on within 3 hours: pending, then ignored.

### Cold-cache alerts

Ignored if the conversation came back cold within 5 minutes of the alert. Acted on if a new conversation started in the same project within 45 minutes. The saving is what resuming would have cost (tokens times price, recorded by the alert) minus the measured cost of the new conversation's first 3 responses. Fewer than 3 responses, or no recorded resume cost: no-data. Under 1 hour old: pending.

### Plan-limit alerts

All sessions together. Compare the spend in the 30 minutes after the alert with the 30 minutes before. Under $0.50 before: no-data. Fewer than 5 responses after: stopped (stopping work is not counted as an effect of the alert). After-spend above 70% of before-spend: ignored. Otherwise counted, and the saving is the difference. This method assumes the earlier pace would have continued; all counted savings of this kind rest on that assumption. Until the 30 minutes are over: pending.

### Not counted twice

A plan-limit saving that overlaps in time with a counted reset or cold-cache saving is overlap, and is not counted.

### Savings can be negative

If the cost went up after the action, the entry is still counted, with a negative saving. It is shown.

### Units

Dollars are API-equivalent at list price. On a subscription a saving is limit kept, not money back. Whether an alert was the reason you acted is not known.

## Which audit rows are alerts

| Kind of alert | Audit row kind | Audit row rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| cold | coach | `cache.cold` |
| reset | coach | `context.reset` |
| reset | finding | `context.window` |
| quota | finding | `quota.*` |

## What these rules do not do

They do not show that an alert caused a change. They show that an alert fired, that the conversation or the spending changed afterwards in a way the rules name, and that a cost measured afterwards was lower. The plan-limit method assumes the earlier pace would have continued. See the README, "What Sparelimit does not claim".
